messages.subject: changing labels with facet_wrap
parts:
Hi all!

I have some plotmath expressions (e.g. NO3- gm-2) (for 10 different
variables) I would like to use as the facet_wrap labels. I have
searched on the web and through the ggplot2 google group and the only
thing I have found was back in 2009 saying that it was on the to do
list.

I was wondering if this issue was updated since then or if there was a
way to work around. I also used facet.grid but I want 10 plots on a
5x2 grid.
thank you in advance
martin

parts:
Hi:

I had to modify your data a bit because you had no observations for
minb, but I got something, at least. The problem does raise the
question of why there is no equivalent labeller = argument in
facet_wrap(), which would be better for your purposes IMO, but to get
expressions in strip labels, you currently have to use facet_grid().
Starting with your input data frame martindf,

mlabels <- levels(martindf$variable2) # hold quoted expressions in a vector
martindfmelt <- melt(martindf, id = c('Treatment', 'variable'),
measure.vars = 'value')
names(martindfmelt) <- c('Treatment', 'variable1', 'variable2', 'value')
# This is a one-level factor that is unneeded, so get rid of it
martindfmelt$variable2 <- NULL
# Recreate the factor variable whose labels are quoted expressions
martindfmelt$variable <- factor(martindfmelt$variable1, labels = mlabels)

ggplot(martindfmelt, aes(x=Treatment, y=value)) +

geom_boxplot(aes(fill=Treatment), notch=FALSE) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="point", shape=5, size=2) +

opts(legend.position="none",
axis.title.x = theme_blank(),
plot.title = theme_text(size=14, lineheight=.8, face="bold"),
strip.background = theme_blank(),
axis.title.x = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_blank()) +

Hi All
to follow-up with my original email. After spending all afternoon on
it I was finally able to change my labels with facet_wrap. For those
interested I used (example for my dataset):

#
#4 plots in this example
#
grob <- ggplotGrob(name_for_original_plot)
strip_elem <- grid.ls(getGrob(grob, "strip.text.x", grep=TRUE,
global=TRUE))$name
#
grob <- grid::editGrob(grob, strip_elem[1],
label=expression(Total~N~(mu*g~g^-1)))
grob <- grid::editGrob(grob, strip_elem[2],
label=expression(Total~C~(mu*g~g^-1)))
grob <- grid::editGrob(grob, strip_elem[3], label=expression(N^15))
grob <- grid::editGrob(grob, strip_elem[4], label=expression(C^14))
grid.draw(grob)
#

thank you
martin
